chunks: 3523 - And it is narrated from Sayf ibn ʿAmīrah, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “Is it permissible for a Muslim to free a slave who is a polytheist?” He said, “No.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh; the Imam being asked, namely Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.سَأَلْتُ: I asked; introduces the legal question directed to the Imam
key_terms.لَا: no; the Imam’s direct negation of permissibility
key_terms.لِلْمُسْلِمِ: for the Muslim; specifies the legal subject addressed by the ruling
key_terms.مَمْلُوكًا: an owned slave; the person being considered for emancipation
key_terms.مُشْرِكًا: a polytheist; identifies the religious status relevant to the ruling
key_terms.يَجُوزُ: is permissible; indicates a fiqh ruling about legal permissibility
key_terms.يُعْتِقَ: to free or emancipate; refers to manumission of a slave

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia fiqh for a Muslim to free a polytheist slave?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling from Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام concerning manumission. It states that it is not permissible for a Muslim to free a slave who is a mushrik.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3523 - It is narrated from Saif bin Amira, who said:
"I asked Abu Abdullah (as), 'Is it permissible for a Muslim to free a slave who is a polytheist?'"
Imam (as) said: "No."
